title: Redirection and Pipes
lead: A pipe connects the output of one command to the input of the next. Small tools combined this way solve big problems.
objectives: You chain commands with `|` into pipelines.
You count, sort and deduplicate with `wc`, `sort` and `uniq`.
You combine pipes and redirection, and split a stream with `tee`.

sections.title: The pipe: command | command
body: `|` connects **stdout** of the left command to **stdin** of the right one. Nothing is written to disk in between. Each tool does one thing; the pipe combines them.
Only stdout travels through a pipe. Error messages (stderr) still go to the screen unless you add `2>&1` before the pipe.

commands.where: At the end of a pipeline to count results.

commands.what: Keeps only lines that match a pattern.
commands.why: Reduces a big stream to the interesting lines.

commands.where: To see the top or bottom of a result.

sections.tip: Build a pipeline step by step: run the first command, check the output, then add the next `|`.

sections.title: sort, uniq and tee
body: `uniq` only collapses **adjacent** duplicate lines, so you almost always run `sort` first. `uniq -c` prefixes each line with its count; `sort -rn` then ranks them by that number.
`sort` compares text by default, so `10` comes before `9`. Use `sort -n` for numbers. `tee file` writes the stream to a file **and** passes it on, like a T-junction.

commands.what: Collapses adjacent duplicates and counts them.
commands.why: Shows how often each line occurs.

commands.what: Saves the stream to a file and also passes it on.
commands.where: To keep an intermediate result of a pipeline.
commands.why: You see and store the data in one go.
commands.example: grep ERROR logs/app.log | tee all_errors.txt | wc -l

sections.warn: `uniq` without `sort` leaves duplicates that are not next to each other.

t01.text: Count the lines of `logs/app.log` with `cat logs/app.log | wc -l`.
t01.hint: The pipe feeds the file content to `wc -l`.

t02.hint: Equal lines appear next to each other.

t03.text: Count how many entries the `data` folder has with `ls -1 data | wc -l`.
t03.hint: `-1` writes each name on its own line; `wc -l` counts the lines.

t04.text: Count the ERROR lines of `logs/app.log` with `grep ERROR logs/app.log | wc -l`.

t05.text: Remove duplicates from `data/fruits.txt` with `sort data/fruits.txt | uniq`.
t05.hint: Sort first so duplicates are adjacent.

t06.text: Count each fruit with `sort data/fruits.txt | uniq -c`.
t06.hint: The number in front is the count.

t07.text: Save all ERROR lines of the log to `errors.txt` with `grep ERROR logs/app.log > errors.txt`.

t08.text: Predict: what is the first line of `sort data/nums.txt | head -n 1`? `2` or `10`? Run it to verify.

t09.text: Predict: which number does `sort -n data/nums.txt | tail -n 1` print? Run it to verify.
t09.hint: `-n` sorts numerically; the last line is the largest.

t10.text: Debug: `uniq data/unsorted.txt` still shows duplicates. Write the unique lines (`a`, `b`) to `~/unique.txt`.

t11.text: Mini project: build the report `report.txt` with the ERROR lines of the log counted and ranked: `grep ERROR logs/app.log | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn > report.txt`.
t11.hint: Four stages: filter, sort, count, rank; then redirect.

t12.text: Challenge: in a single pipeline save all ERROR lines to `all_errors.txt` and also print how many there are (use `tee`).

t13.text: Ticket: Management wants to know how many different users appear in `data/access.txt`. Write only the number into `~/users_count.txt`.

vm.intro: On your VM these pipelines only read; the only files written are ones you create in your home directory.

v01.title: Count with a pipe
v01.text: Count how many entries `/etc` has and paste the number.
differs: The number depends on your system; any number is fine.

v02.title: Extract and sort users
v02.text: Take the first field of `/etc/passwd`, sort it and show the first five names.
differs: Names differ per distribution; only the alphabetical order matters. Use `| grep root` to check that `root` exists.

v03.title: Frequency table
v03.text: Count which login shells are used in `/etc/passwd` and rank them.
differs: Counts and shells vary per system.
If you see only one line, check that `sort` comes before `uniq -c`.

v04.title: Keep a copy with tee
v04.text: Save a listing with `tee` while counting it; check the file. If it worked press "Done".
differs: If `etc_list.txt` is empty, check that you wrote `~/etc_list.txt` after `tee`.

options: stdout of the left command to stdin of the right command
q1.explain: The pipe feeds the left command's stdout into the right command's stdin.

q3.q: What does `tee out.txt` do in a pipeline?
options: Writes the stream to a file and passes it on
q3.explain: `tee` splits the stream like a T-piece.

q4.q: Which command prints the largest number of a file with one number per line?
q4.explain: `sort -n` ranks numerically; the last line is the largest.

summary: `cmd1 | cmd2` passes stdout of cmd1 as stdin to cmd2.
`sort | uniq -c | sort -rn` builds a frequency ranking.
`sort -n` sorts numerically; plain `sort` sorts as text.
`tee` stores a stream in a file while passing it on.

glossary.meaning: Connects the output of one command to the input of another.
A chain of commands joined by pipes.
A command that reads stdin and writes a changed stream to stdout.
Writes a stream to a file and to stdout.
